LR statistic of `r format(round(local_anchor_lr$LR,1),big.mark=',')` and a much
lower AIC. The conditional profile peaks near 0.35. Reporting-parameter fits
started near 0.02, the conditional optimum, and 0.65; the low and high screens
are respectively
`r format(round(max(local_anchor_refinement$loglik)-
  local_anchor_refinement$loglik[local_anchor_refinement$stage=='low'],1),
  big.mark=',')` and
`r format(round(max(local_anchor_refinement$loglik)-
  local_anchor_refinement$loglik[local_anchor_refinement$stage=='high'],1),
  big.mark=',')` likelihood points below the best result. A central-difference
reporting block improves the main forward result and a separate transition-
hazard block adds only
`r sprintf('%.2f',local_anchor_refinement$loglik[
  local_anchor_refinement$stage=='transition']-
  local_anchor_refinement$loglik[local_anchor_refinement$stage=='central'])`
points. The blocks are deliberately short and retain convergence code 1, so
this is strong multistart evidence but not a claim of final full convergence.

Entry changes from 2.308% to
`r sprintf('%.3f',100*local_anchor_comparison$entry_rate[3])`% and exit from
4.142% to `r sprintf('%.3f',100*local_anchor_comparison$exit_rate[3])`%.
Status error also remains near 2.96%. The new channel therefore changes the
measurement process while leaving the paper's transition interpretation
essentially intact.

\clearpage

```{r local-anchor-predictive}
local_metrics <- c("exact_continuation","local_revision_1_to_6_months",
  "whole_year_revision","other_revision")
local_labels <- c("Exact continuation","Local revision (1 to 6 months)",
  "Whole-year revision","Other revision")
lp <- local_anchor_predictive[
  local_anchor_predictive$metric %in% local_metrics,]
lp <- lp[order(match(lp$metric,local_metrics),lp$model),]
lp_show <- data.frame(Measure=rep(local_labels,each=2),Model=lp$model,
  Predicted=sprintf("%.2f",100*lp$predicted_mean),
  Observed=sprintf("%.2f",100*lp$observed),check.names=FALSE)
knitr::kable(lp_show,booktabs=TRUE,
  caption="Predictive implications of local anchor revisions (percent)")
```

The old exact-anchor model predicts only
`r sprintf('%.1f',100*lp$predicted_mean[lp$model=='Exact-anchor model' &
  lp$metric=='local_revision_1_to_6_months'])`% local revisions, compared with
`r sprintf('%.1f',100*lp$observed[lp$metric==
  'local_revision_1_to_6_months'][1])`% observed. The extension raises the
prediction to
`r sprintf('%.1f',100*lp$predicted_mean[lp$model=='Local anchor revisions' &
  lp$metric=='local_revision_1_to_6_months'])`%. Local-only records contribute
`r format(round(local_anchor_decomposition$loglik_gain[
  local_anchor_decomposition$pattern=='Local revision only']),big.mark=',')`
likelihood points and mixed-pattern records contribute another
`r format(round(local_anchor_decomposition$loglik_gain[
  local_anchor_decomposition$pattern=='Mixed']),big.mark=',')`; losses on
other and whole-year-only records partly offset these gains. This confirms
that the extension improves the feature it was designed to capture rather
than obtaining its fit from unrelated observations.

The check is not yet fully satisfactory. Exact continuations remain
underpredicted (about 61.7% versus 64.7%), local revisions remain slightly
underpredicted (10.8% versus 11.4%), and residual revisions remain
overpredicted (22.2% versus 16.9%). Whole-year revisions now fall below the
observed share. The fixed local kernel is therefore a useful first repair, not
a complete reporting model. Holding all other parameters fixed, the local
probability has a curvature-based standard error of
`r sprintf('%.3f',100*local_anchor_curvature$se_probability)` percentage
points and a 95% interval of
[`r sprintf('%.2f',100*local_anchor_curvature$lower_probability)`%,
`r sprintf('%.2f',100*local_anchor_curvature$upper_probability)`%]. This is
conditional rather than full nuisance-adjusted inference and should not be
used as the final paper standard error.

\clearpage

### Shared person-level duration-reporting reliability

The next extension allows tenure and timegap reports from the same person to
share a latent propensity for contamination. Each person belongs with equal
prior probability to a reliable or unreliable reporting class. Relative to a
common midpoint, the reliable class shifts both contamination logits down by
$\delta$ and the unreliable class shifts them up by $\delta$. Thus
$\delta=0$ reproduces the preceding independent-reporting likelihood exactly.
The fixed equal class shares keep this first extension parsimonious and avoid
an additional mixing-proportion parameter and label switching.

```{r shared-reliability-comparison}
sr <- shared_reliability_comparison[c(1,3),]
shared_show <- data.frame(
  Quantity=c("Entry","Exit","Status error","Job reset",
    "Exact-anchor retention","Local revision",
    "Reliability-logit dispersion","Log likelihood","AIC"),
  Independent=c(sprintf("%.3f",100*c(sr$entry_rate[1],sr$exit_rate[1],
    sr$status_misclassification[1],sr$job_change_prob[1],
    sr$exact_anchor_retention_prob[1],sr$local_anchor_revision_prob[1])),
    "0.000",format(round(sr$loglik[1],1),big.mark=",",scientific=FALSE),
    format(round(sr$AIC[1],1),big.mark=",",scientific=FALSE)),
  `Shared reliability`=c(sprintf("%.3f",100*c(sr$entry_rate[2],
    sr$exit_rate[2],sr$status_misclassification[2],sr$job_change_prob[2],
    sr$exact_anchor_retention_prob[2],sr$local_anchor_revision_prob[2])),
    sprintf("%.3f",sr$duration_reliability_shift[2]),
    format(round(sr$loglik[2],1),big.mark=",",scientific=FALSE),
    format(round(sr$AIC[2],1),big.mark=",",scientific=FALSE)),
  check.names=FALSE)
knitr::kable(shared_show,booktabs=TRUE,
  caption="Shared duration-reporting reliability (rates in percent)")
```

The likelihood rises by
`r format(round(diff(sr$loglik),1),big.mark=',')` points with one additional
parameter, while entry remains `r sprintf('%.3f',100*sr$entry_rate[2])`% and
exit remains `r sprintf('%.3f',100*sr$exit_rate[2])`%. The reporting extension
therefore leaves the substantive transition estimates essentially unchanged.
The exact equality of the two likelihoods at $\delta=0$ was verified
numerically. The LR statistic is
`r format(round(shared_reliability_lr$LR,1),big.mark=',')`, but its usual
one-degree-of-freedom chi-squared reference distribution is not valid because
the null is a homogeneous-mixture boundary. Final inference requires a
parametric bootstrap.

```{r shared-reliability-components}
component_show <- data.frame(
  Class=c("Reliable","Unreliable","Equal-prior marginal mean"),
  `Prior share`=c(sprintf("%.1f",100*
    shared_reliability_components$prior_probability),"--"),
  `Tenure contamination`=sprintf("%.2f",100*c(
    shared_reliability_components$tenure_contamination,
    mean(shared_reliability_components$tenure_contamination))),
  `Timegap contamination`=sprintf("%.2f",100*c(
    shared_reliability_components$timegap_contamination,
    mean(shared_reliability_components$timegap_contamination))),
  check.names=FALSE)
knitr::kable(component_show,booktabs=TRUE,
  caption="Implied duration-contamination probabilities by latent reliability class (percent)")
```

The reliable class has tenure and timegap contamination probabilities of
`r sprintf('%.2f',100*shared_reliability_components$tenure_contamination[1])`%
and
`r sprintf('%.2f',100*shared_reliability_components$timegap_contamination[1])`%,
compared with
`r sprintf('%.2f',100*shared_reliability_components$tenure_contamination[2])`%
and
`r sprintf('%.2f',100*shared_reliability_components$timegap_contamination[2])`%
in the unreliable class. The survey-weighted mean posterior probability of
the unreliable class is
`r sprintf('%.1f',100*shared_reliability_posterior$posterior_unreliable[shared_reliability_posterior$statistic=='weighted mean'])`%,
with a median of
`r sprintf('%.1f',100*shared_reliability_posterior$posterior_unreliable[shared_reliability_posterior$statistic=='median'])`%.
The midpoint contamination parameters reported by the optimizer are not
population-average probabilities in this mixture; the class-specific values
and equal-prior marginal means above are the interpretable quantities.

All three deliberately dispersed joint starts improve on the independent
model. The best low and high starts remain respectively
`r format(round(max(shared_reliability_refinement$loglik)-shared_reliability_refinement$loglik[shared_reliability_refinement$stage=='low'],1),big.mark=',')`
and
`r format(round(max(shared_reliability_refinement$loglik)-shared_reliability_refinement$loglik[shared_reliability_refinement$stage=='high'],1),big.mark=',')`
likelihood points below the preferred basin. The short joint blocks terminate
at their iteration caps, however, so the result is a strong provisional point
estimate rather than a final convergence claim.

```{r shared-reliability-predictive}
shared_metrics <- c("exact_continuation","local_revision_1_to_6_months",
  "other_revision","timegap_inconsistent",
  "two_opportunities_no_irregularity",
  "two_opportunities_one_irregularity",
  "two_opportunities_two_irregularities")
shared_labels <- c("Exact continuation","Local revision (1 to 6 months)",
  "Other revision","Timegap inconsistency",
  "Two opportunities: no irregularity",
  "Two opportunities: one irregularity",
  "Two opportunities: two irregularities")
sp <- shared_reliability_predictive[
  shared_reliability_predictive$metric %in% shared_metrics,]
sp$label <- shared_labels[match(sp$metric,shared_metrics)]
sp_wide <- reshape(sp[,c("label","model","predicted_mean")],
  idvar="label",timevar="model",direction="wide")
sp_obs <- sp[!duplicated(sp$label),c("label","observed")]
sp_wide <- merge(sp_obs,sp_wide,by="label",sort=FALSE)
sp_wide <- sp_wide[match(shared_labels,sp_wide$label),]
shared_pred_show <- data.frame(
  Measure=sp_wide$label,Observed=sprintf("%.2f",100*sp_wide$observed),
  Independent=sprintf("%.2f",100*sp_wide$`predicted_mean.Independent reliability`),
  `Shared reliability`=sprintf("%.2f",100*sp_wide$`predicted_mean.Shared reliability`),
  check.names=FALSE)
knitr::kable(shared_pred_show,booktabs=TRUE,
  caption="Predictive implications of shared reporting reliability (percent)")
```

Shared reliability improves the local-revision prediction from 10.77% to
11.13% against 11.43% observed and moves the repeated-opportunity distribution
in the right direction: the predicted shares with no and exactly one
irregularity change from 60.36% and 24.07% to 62.88% and 19.39%, against
68.05% and 16.43% observed. It is not a complete repair. The model raises the
two-irregularity share from 15.58% to 17.73% against 15.52% observed, and the
exact, residual-revision, and timegap moments remain outside their simulation
intervals.

The likelihood decomposition confirms that the improvement is concentrated
where duration information is informative: records with no irregularity,
tenure deviations, and timegap inconsistencies account for 65.6%, 28.9%, and
5.8% of the gain, respectively. The average posterior unreliable probability
is 28.0% for regular repeated-state records, 87.5% for tenure deviations, and
92.6% for timegap inconsistencies.

There is an important identification limitation. Across only three waves, a
record cannot contain both a repeated employed spell and a repeated
nonemployment spell. The common shift across tenure and timegap is therefore
not identified from observing both clocks repeatedly for the same person.
Instead, it is a parsimonious cross-clock restriction learned indirectly from
serial clustering within each clock. The following specification check allows
separate tenure- and timegap-reliability dispersions and tests whether the
common-shift restriction is supported.

\clearpage

#### Relaxing the common-shift restriction

The restriction test replaces the single $\delta$ with separate nonnegative
tenure and timegap dispersions, while retaining the same person-level class
and equal prior shares. Setting the two dispersions equal reproduces the
common-shift likelihood exactly; this was verified to numerical precision.

```{r separate-reliability-comparison}
sep <- separate_reliability_comparison
separate_show <- data.frame(
  Quantity=c("Entry","Exit","Status error","Job reset",
    "Exact-anchor retention","Local revision","Tenure dispersion",
    "Timegap dispersion","Log likelihood","AIC"),
  `Common dispersion`=c(sprintf("%.3f",100*c(sep$entry_rate[1],
    sep$exit_rate[1],sep$status_misclassification[1],
    sep$job_change_prob[1],sep$exact_anchor_retention_prob[1],
    sep$local_anchor_revision_prob[1])),
    sprintf("%.3f",c(sep$tenure_reliability_shift[1],
      sep$timegap_reliability_shift[1])),
    format(round(sep$loglik[1],1),big.mark=",",scientific=FALSE),
    format(round(sep$AIC[1],1),big.mark=",",scientific=FALSE)),
  `Separate dispersions`=c(sprintf("%.3f",100*c(sep$entry_rate[2],
    sep$exit_rate[2],sep$status_misclassification[2],
    sep$job_change_prob[2],sep$exact_anchor_retention_prob[2],
    sep$local_anchor_revision_prob[2])),
    sprintf("%.3f",c(sep$tenure_reliability_shift[2],
      sep$timegap_reliability_shift[2])),
    format(round(sep$loglik[2],1),big.mark=",",scientific=FALSE),
    format(round(sep$AIC[2],1),big.mark=",",scientific=FALSE)),
  check.names=FALSE)
knitr::kable(separate_show,booktabs=TRUE,
  caption="Relaxing equal tenure and timegap reliability dispersions (rates in percent)")
```

The estimated tenure dispersion is
`r sprintf('%.3f',sep$tenure_reliability_shift[2])`, compared with
`r sprintf('%.3f',sep$timegap_reliability_shift[2])` for timegap. The log
likelihood rises by
`r format(round(diff(sep$loglik),1),big.mark=',')` points and AIC falls by
`r format(round(-diff(sep$AIC),1),big.mark=',')`. The equality-restriction LR
statistic is `r format(round(separate_reliability_lr$LR,1),big.mark=',')` on
one degree of freedom. This is a like-for-like comparison: the unrestricted
fit was continued jointly until a further step made no improvement, the
restricted fit was initialized by projecting those nuisance estimates onto a
common shift, its common shift was polished conditionally, and a final full
restricted step also made no improvement. Both retained fits have convergence
code zero. The earlier unrefined LR statistic was much larger because it
incorrectly attributed unrelated nuisance-parameter refinement to the single
dispersion restriction.

Entry and exit remain
`r sprintf('%.3f',100*sep$entry_rate[2])`% and
`r sprintf('%.3f',100*sep$exit_rate[2])`%. Relaxing the restriction therefore
changes the duration-reporting decomposition without changing the paper's
substantive employment-transition estimates.

```{r separate-reliability-components}
separate_component_show <- data.frame(
  Class=c("Reliable","Unreliable","Equal-prior marginal mean"),
  `Prior share`=c(sprintf("%.1f",100*
    separate_reliability_components$prior_probability),"--"),
  `Tenure contamination`=sprintf("%.2f",100*c(
    separate_reliability_components$tenure_contamination,
    mean(separate_reliability_components$tenure_contamination))),
  `Timegap contamination`=sprintf("%.2f",100*c(
    separate_reliability_components$timegap_contamination,
    mean(separate_reliability_components$timegap_contamination))),
  check.names=FALSE)
knitr::kable(separate_component_show,booktabs=TRUE,
  caption="Contamination probabilities under separate reliability dispersions (percent)")
```

The unrestricted model sharpens the tenure separation: tenure contamination
is `r sprintf('%.2f',100*separate_reliability_components$tenure_contamination[1])`%
in the reliable class and
`r sprintf('%.2f',100*separate_reliability_components$tenure_contamination[2])`%
in the unreliable class. The corresponding timegap probabilities are
`r sprintf('%.2f',100*separate_reliability_components$timegap_contamination[1])`%
and
`r sprintf('%.2f',100*separate_reliability_components$timegap_contamination[2])`%.
The survey-weighted
mean posterior unreliable probability is
`r sprintf('%.1f',100*separate_reliability_posterior$posterior_unreliable[separate_reliability_posterior$statistic=='weighted mean'])`%.

```{r separate-reliability-inference}
inference_labels <- c(
  entry_rate="Entry rate",exit_rate="Exit rate",
  status_misclassification="Status error",
  reliable_tenure="Tenure contamination: reliable",
  unreliable_tenure="Tenure contamination: unreliable",
  reliable_timegap="Timegap contamination: reliable",
  unreliable_timegap="Timegap contamination: unreliable",
  tenure_reliability_shift="Tenure dispersion",
  timegap_reliability_shift="Timegap dispersion",
  shift_difference="Timegap minus tenure dispersion")
sir <- separate_reliability_inference[
  separate_reliability_inference$quantity %in% names(inference_labels),]
sir <- sir[match(names(inference_labels),sir$quantity),]
probability <- !sir$quantity %in% c("tenure_reliability_shift",
  "timegap_reliability_shift","shift_difference")
scale <- ifelse(probability,100,1)
inference_show <- data.frame(
  Quantity=unname(inference_labels[sir$quantity]),
  Estimate=sprintf("%.3f",scale*sir$estimate),
  `OPG standard error`=sprintf("(%.3f)",scale*sir$se),check.names=FALSE)
knitr::kable(inference_show,booktabs=TRUE,
  caption="Provisional full-nuisance OPG inference (rates in percent)")
```

The 33-parameter OPG matrix is full rank and positive definite, but its
condition number is
`r format(round(separate_reliability_information$condition_number),big.mark=',')`.
The fourth exit-hazard perturbation required a tenfold smaller finite-
difference step. Most importantly, the OPG Wald interval for the difference
between the two dispersions includes zero even though the directly optimized
LR statistic is large. The OPG is an outer-product approximation rather than
the exact observed Hessian, and the mixture likelihood is evidently not well
approximated by one common local quadratic for this contrast. The LR comparison
is therefore the preferred evidence about the equality restriction; the OPG
errors are useful provisional uncertainty measures for the headline rates but
not a substitute for a profile or bootstrap of the dispersion difference.

```{r separate-reliability-profile}
srpi <- separate_reliability_profile_interval[1,]
profile_show <- data.frame(
  Quantity=c("Timegap minus tenure dispersion","95% profile interval",
    "LR test of equal dispersions","LR p-value"),
  Result=c(sprintf("%.4f",srpi$estimate),
    sprintf("[%.4f, %.4f]",srpi$profile_lower,srpi$profile_upper),
    sprintf("%.2f",srpi$equality_LR),
    format(srpi$equality_p_value,digits=3,scientific=TRUE)))
knitr::kable(profile_show,booktabs=TRUE,
  caption="Nuisance-adjusted profile inference for the dispersion difference")
```

The direct profile fixes the timegap-minus-tenure dispersion difference and
reoptimizes the other 32 parameters. Each outer bracket was screened from a
nearby solution and from the common-dispersion nuisance estimates; all
retained fits converged, and the nearby starts gave the higher likelihood on
both sides. Tightly optimized points near both confidence limits
give a 95% profile interval from
`r sprintf('%.4f',srpi$profile_lower)` to
`r sprintf('%.4f',srpi$profile_upper)`, which excludes zero by a wide margin.
The profile therefore agrees with the fully optimized LR test and shows that
the broad OPG Wald interval is a numerical/local-quadratic failure for this
specific contrast. It does not invalidate the provisional OPG uncertainty
measures for the headline transition rates.

A 10,000-person simulation-recovery check held the remaining nuisance
parameters at their generating values and estimated the two midpoints and two
dispersions from three widely separated starts. All starts converged to the
same likelihood. Tenure midpoint and dispersion biases were
`r sprintf('%+.3f',100*(separate_reliability_recovery$eps-
  separate_reliability_comparison$tenure_contamination_midpoint[2]))`
percentage points and
`r sprintf('%+.3f',separate_reliability_recovery$tenure_reliability_shift-
  separate_reliability_comparison$tenure_reliability_shift[2])`;
timegap was noisier, with corresponding biases of
`r sprintf('%+.3f',100*(separate_reliability_recovery$eps_d-
  separate_reliability_comparison$timegap_contamination_midpoint[2]))`
points and
`r sprintf('%+.3f',separate_reliability_recovery$timegap_reliability_shift-
  separate_reliability_comparison$timegap_reliability_shift[2])`.
The posterior reliability score classified the simulated latent groups with
AUC `r sprintf('%.3f',separate_reliability_recovery$AUC)`. This is encouraging
but remains a one-replication, conditional recovery diagnostic rather than a
complete finite-sample validation of all 33 parameters.

```{r separate-reliability-predictive}
sep_metrics <- c("exact_continuation","local_revision_1_to_6_months",
  "other_revision","timegap_inconsistent",
  "two_opportunities_no_irregularity",
  "two_opportunities_one_irregularity",
  "two_opportunities_two_irregularities")
sep_labels <- c("Exact continuation","Local revision (1 to 6 months)",
  "Other revision","Timegap inconsistency",
  "Two opportunities: no irregularity",
  "Two opportunities: one irregularity",
  "Two opportunities: two irregularities")
spp <- separate_reliability_predictive[
  separate_reliability_predictive$metric %in% sep_metrics,]
spp$label <- sep_labels[match(spp$metric,sep_metrics)]
spp_wide <- reshape(spp[,c("label","model","predicted_mean")],
  idvar="label",timevar="model",direction="wide")
spp_obs <- spp[!duplicated(spp$label),c("label","observed")]
spp_wide <- merge(spp_obs,spp_wide,by="label",sort=FALSE)
spp_wide <- spp_wide[match(sep_labels,spp_wide$label),]
separate_pred_show <- data.frame(
  Measure=spp_wide$label,Observed=sprintf("%.2f",100*spp_wide$observed),
  `Common dispersion`=sprintf("%.2f",100*
    spp_wide$`predicted_mean.Common dispersion`),
  `Separate dispersions`=sprintf("%.2f",100*
    spp_wide$`predicted_mean.Separate dispersions`),check.names=FALSE)
knitr::kable(separate_pred_show,booktabs=TRUE,
  caption="Predictive implications of separate reliability dispersions (percent)")
```

Separate dispersions improve exact continuations from 63.8% to 64.1% against
64.7% observed. They change the predicted share with two regular duration
opportunities from 65.0% to 64.8% against 68.1%, and increase predicted
timegap inconsistencies from 16.6% to 17.1% against 15.5%. The local-revision
prediction also moves away from its observed value, and all reported moments
remain outside the simulation intervals. The extension is preferred by the
observed likelihood, but is not an adequate reporting model on these coarse
predictive checks.

The likelihood decomposition makes the tradeoff explicit. Regular
repeated-state records lose about 591 likelihood points relative to the
fully refined common-dispersion model, tenure deviations lose about 559, and
records without repeated-state duration information lose about 9. These are
more than offset by a gain of about 1,231 among timegap-inconsistent records.
Thus the likelihood improvement comes from fitting the distribution within
the timegap-inconsistent group, not from reducing its aggregate predicted
frequency.

# 6. Script and output register

**`diagnostics/audit_job_start_dates.R`.** Implemented. Reconstructs
reported start months and audits heaping, revisions, persistence, and matching
sensitivity. It is a base-R script, accepts an A/B/C panel path, and writes
panel-specific and combined outputs.

**`EM-tenure/R/job_change_eps.R`.** Implemented. Enumerates same-job and
new-job branches inside full latent employment spells, exactly nests the old
emission at (q=0), uses log-sum-exp, and exposes posterior job-change counts.

**`EM-tenure/estimate_job_change_tenure_contamination.R`.** Implemented.
Profiles (q), jointly estimates it with all nuisance parameters, rejects an
invalid or inferior fit, and preserves the preferred Table 7 fit as the nested
comparison. It does not bootstrap.

**`EM-tenure/estimate_job_change_matching_robustness.R`.** Implemented.
Re-estimates the identical 15-parameter model on Panels B and C from the Panel
A optimum and writes separate robustness outputs without replacing the main
fit.

**`EM-tenure/validate_job_change_model.R`.** Implemented. Runs dispersed
starts, tight refinement, a nuisance-adjusted profile, multistart full-model
recovery simulations, and a large-sample score diagnostic. The recovery check
currently fails and identifies the monthly-mass repair as the next priority.

**`EM-tenure/R/tenure_monthly_eps.R`.** Implemented. Replaces continuous
tenure densities with monthly probability masses, advances clean clocks by
three months, and uses a discrete 0--2 month support for entries and resets.

**`EM-tenure/validate_monthly_tenure_model.R`.** Implemented. Checks mass
normalization, evaluates large-sample scores, and re-estimates simulated data
from dispersed starts. The first full-likelihood recovery exercise is close to
the generating parameters.

**`EM-tenure/validate_monthly_tenure_recovery_grid.R`.** Implemented. Runs a
resumable recovery grid at multiple sample sizes, repeats dispersed-start
checks, and reports bias, RMSE, hazard recovery, and likelihood scores.

**`EM-tenure/estimate_monthly_job_change_tenure_contamination.R`.**
Implemented. Preserves reported zero-month tenure, estimates the no-reset and
reset models on Panel A, and compares three reset starting values.

**`EM-tenure/estimate_monthly_job_change_matching_robustness.R`.**
Implemented. Re-estimates the corrected monthly model on Panels B and C,
checks the monthly grid, screens low, main, and high reset starts, and writes
separate cached robustness outputs without replacing Panel A.

**`EM-tenure/estimate_monthly_persistent_tenure_reporting.R`.** Implemented.
Adds a within-job retain-versus-redraw process for consecutive gross tenure
reports, checks exact nesting, screens three persistence starts, and retains
the exact boundary fit when all positive approximations are inferior.

**`EM-tenure/validate_monthly_persistent_tenure_reporting.R`.** Implemented.
Simulates positive persistence, evaluates a conditional profile, and performs
two full-likelihood recovery fits from dispersed starts.

**`EM-tenure/estimate_monthly_calendar_heaping.R`.** Implemented. Retains the
nominal interview quarter, adds a normalized January-conditioned component to
gross tenure reports, verifies exact nesting, and screens three Panel A starts.

**`EM-tenure/validate_monthly_calendar_heaping.R`.** Implemented. Simulates a
positive January-heaping probability, evaluates its conditional likelihood,
and checks joint recovery from low and high starts.

**`EM-tenure/infer_monthly_calendar_heaping.R`.** Implemented. Evaluates the
full numerical observed-information matrix in resumable parallel chunks and
uses the delta method for the reported rates and calendar-heaping quantities.

**`EM-tenure/estimate_monthly_calendar_revision.R`.** Implemented. Adds a
normalized, correlated whole-year revision branch to eligible consecutive
gross reports, verifies exact nesting, and screens three Panel A starts.

**`EM-tenure/validate_monthly_calendar_revision.R`.** Implemented. Verifies
conditional identification and joint recovery of whole-year revision and
January-heaping probabilities from dispersed starts.

**`EM-tenure/infer_monthly_calendar_revision.R`.** Implemented. Computes the
full 17-parameter observed-information matrix in resumable parallel chunks and
uses the delta method for all reported rates.

**`EM-tenure/profile_monthly_calendar_revision.R`.** Implemented. Reoptimizes
all nuisance parameters from warm and alternative starts on both sides of the
whole-year revision estimate and interpolates the 95% profile interval.

**`EM-tenure/diagnose_monthly_calendar_revision.R`.** Implemented. Simulates
calendar moments at fitted parameters and decomposes the exact observed-data
likelihood gain by mutually exclusive observed patterns.

**`EM-tenure/estimate_monthly_clean_anchor_revision.R`.** Implemented. Adds a
separate whole-year revision probability for a current gross report following
a clean reported date, verifies exact nesting, and screens three starts.

**`EM-tenure/validate_monthly_clean_anchor_revision.R`.** Implemented. Checks
the conditional likelihood and joint recovery of clean-anchor, gross-anchor,
and January-heaping probabilities from two dispersed starts.

**`EM-tenure/diagnose_monthly_clean_anchor_revision.R`.** Implemented. Compares
fitted calendar moments with the nested model and decomposes the row-level
likelihood gain by observable report patterns.

**`EM-tenure/estimate_monthly_start_month_baseline.R`.** Implemented. Adds 11
month logits shared by clean and gross marginal reports, verifies exact nesting
at equal probabilities, screens three conditional starts, and performs staged
joint Panel A refinement.

**`EM-tenure/refine_monthly_start_month_baseline.R`.** Implemented. Continues
the full-sample central-difference refinement without repeating the conditional
mode search.

**`EM-tenure/diagnose_monthly_start_month_baseline.R`.** Implemented. Compares
the full fitted month distribution and consecutive-report patterns with the
nested model and decomposes the likelihood gain by observed start month.

**`EM-tenure/validate_monthly_start_month_baseline.R`.** Implemented. Checks
distant month-distribution starts and joint recovery, including a safeguarded
one-sided gradient near the zero-heaping boundary.

**`EM-tenure/estimate_monthly_exact_anchor_retention.R`.** Implemented. Adds a
single retain-versus-revise/redraw channel after either a clean or gross
reported anchor, verifies exact nesting, profiles the new parameter widely,
and performs staged joint refinement plus a conditional polish.

**`EM-tenure/diagnose_monthly_exact_anchor_retention.R`.** Implemented.
Compares exact, whole-year, and other consecutive-report changes with fitted
simulations and decomposes the observed likelihood gain by report pattern.

**`EM-tenure/validate_monthly_exact_anchor_retention.R`.** Implemented. Runs
20 conditional recovery samples at the empirical generating value and records
bias, RMSE, range, and the LR statistic against zero.

**`EM-tenure/refine_monthly_exact_anchor_retention.R`.** Implemented. Resumes
the saved 30-parameter fit, compares continued, low-retention, and
high-retention starts, promotes the best joint fit, and finishes with an exact
conditional polish without discarding cached work.

**`EM-tenure/validate_monthly_exact_anchor_joint_recovery.R`.** Implemented.
Simulates the complete model and re-estimates all 30 parameters from near and
dispersed starts, with resumable replication caches and separate summaries of
transition, hazard, calendar-baseline, and reporting-process recovery.

**`EM-tenure/infer_monthly_exact_anchor_retention_opg.R`.** Implemented. Uses
61 finite-difference likelihood evaluations and record-level scores to obtain
a full-rank OPG information approximation, delta-method errors, boundary
flags, and correlations among natural-scale reporting probabilities.

**`EM-tenure/infer_monthly_exact_anchor_retention.R`.** Implemented as a
resumable exact central observed-Hessian calculation. It requires 1,801 full
likelihood evaluations; 48 are currently cached, so this remains a
confirmatory calculation rather than the reported inference result.

**`EM-tenure/estimate_monthly_local_anchor_revision.R`.** Implemented. Adds a
normalized one-to-six-month revision kernel conditional on not retaining the
preceding anchor exactly. It verifies exact nesting, profiles the new
probability, screens low and high starts, refines the competing reporting
parameters, checks the transition-hazard block, and caches every completed
stage. The calendar fitter now accepts named free-parameter blocks while
retaining its full-fit default.

**`EM-tenure/diagnose_monthly_local_anchor_revision.R`.** Implemented. Compares
exact, local, whole-year, and residual revisions in observed and simulated
data, decomposes the likelihood gain by report pattern, and reports a clearly
labelled conditional-curvature approximation for the new probability.

**`EM-tenure/estimate_monthly_shared_duration_reliability.R`.** Implemented.
Adds an equal-weight person-level reliability mixture shared by tenure and
timegap contamination, verifies exact nesting at zero dispersion, profiles
the new parameter, and performs resumable dispersed-start joint refinement.

**`EM-tenure/diagnose_monthly_shared_duration_reliability.R`.** Implemented.
Compares observed and fitted duration-irregularity patterns, decomposes the
row-level likelihood gain, and summarizes posterior unreliable-class
probabilities without interpreting class membership as an observed trait.

**`EM-tenure/estimate_monthly_separate_duration_reliability.R`.** Implemented.
Allows tenure and timegap contamination to have separate reliability
dispersions, verifies exact nesting when they are equal, maps the conditional
surface, and screens common and asymmetric starts before a conditional polish.

**`EM-tenure/diagnose_monthly_separate_duration_reliability.R`.** Implemented.
Compares fitted duration-pattern distributions under common and separate
dispersions and decomposes their row-level likelihood difference.

**Separate-reliability refinements.** Implemented in:

```
EM-tenure/refine_monthly_separate_duration_reliability.R
```

Project the converged nuisance estimates into the equality-restricted model,

**`EM-tenure/validate_monthly_separate_duration_reliability.R`.** Implemented.
Runs cached multiple-start conditional recovery simulations for the two

**`EM-tenure/infer_monthly_separate_duration_reliability_opg.R`.** Implemented.

**Separate-reliability profile.** Implemented in:

```
EM-tenure/profile_monthly_separate_duration_reliability.R
EM-tenure/refine_monthly_separate_duration_reliability_profile_limits.R
```

Reparameterize the clock-specific dispersions by their average
and fixed difference, screen both profile sides from distinct nuisance starts,

**[Analytical-inference script](../EM-tenure/infer_monthly_job_change_tenure_contamination.R).** Implemented.
Computes the full observed-information matrix in parallel, propagates it to

**[Profile-refinement script](../EM-tenure/refine_monthly_profile_point.R).**

**`EM-tenure/tests/testthat/test-job-change-eps.R`.** Implemented. Covers

# 7. Acceptance checks for the first extension

The first empirical result should not be added to Table 7 until all of the
following are complete. Checks already passed are marked accordingly:

- exact equality to the existing likelihood at (q=0) --- **passed**;
- finite likelihoods at interior (q) values and valid posterior probabilities
  --- **passed**;
- optimizer convergence from the nested fit --- **passed**;
- no deterioration relative to the nested model --- **passed**;
- recovery of (q) in a simplified emission simulation --- **passed**;
- dispersed starts and tighter tolerances --- **passed**, with an inferior
  low-reset local mode that makes multistart selection necessary;
- recovery of (q) and nuisance parameters in full-likelihood simulations ---
  **failed** under the current continuous-density approximation;
- discrete monthly masses sum to one and zero-month reports are retained ---
  **passed**;
- discrete-month full-likelihood recovery from dispersed starts ---
  **passed** in six repeated fits at 10,000 and 40,000 observations, with bias
  and RMSE contracting at the larger sample;
- discrete-month Panel A convergence from low, main, and high reset starts ---
  **passed**, with closely agreeing estimates and log likelihoods;
- matching-panel sensitivity --- **passed** for both the continuous diagnostic
  and the corrected discrete model; all B/C starts converge, while reset and
  contamination estimates decline monotonically with stricter matching; and
- full-rank positive-definite observed information and delta-method errors ---
  **passed**; and
- nuisance-adjusted profile-likelihood inference --- **passed**, with all
  retained points converged and a profile interval nearly identical to the
  analytical interval; and
- positive persistence recoverability --- **passed provisionally** in one
  12,000-record simulation; both joint starts identify substantial positive
  persistence, although additional replications are required to characterize
  its finite-sample bias; and
- January-heaping normalization, nesting, recovery, and Panel A multistart
  convergence --- **passed**; all three empirical starts estimate about 24%
  conditional heaping, and a 6,000-record simulation closely recovers a 40%
  generating probability; and
- January-heaping observed-information inference --- **passed**; the full
  16-parameter information matrix is positive definite and full rank; and
- whole-year revision normalization, nesting, recovery, and Panel A multistart
  convergence --- **passed**; the recovery exercise separates the revision
  and January-heaping components, and the empirical results are reported
  above;
- whole-year revision observed-information and nuisance-profile inference ---
  **passed**; the information matrix is full rank and positive definite, and
  the two interval estimates agree closely; and
- whole-year revision predictive adequacy --- **failed**; the extension moves
  the targeted moment in the correct direction but materially underpredicts
  both January starts and whole-year revisions, while its positive likelihood
  gain is concentrated in 6.16% of weighted records;
- clean-anchor revision nesting, multistart convergence, and joint recovery
  --- **passed provisionally**; three empirical starts agree and two simulated
  starts recover both revision channels, although an 8,000-record exercise
  shows offsetting finite-sample bias between them;
- clean-anchor observed-information inference --- **passed**; the full
  18-parameter matrix is positive definite and full rank; and
- clean-anchor predictive adequacy --- **failed but improved**; the predicted
  whole-year revision share moves from 4.10% to 5.79% against 7.01% observed,
  while January starts and exact continuations remain poorly reproduced;
- shared baseline start-month normalization and exact nesting --- **passed**;
  equal probabilities reproduce the 18-parameter model exactly and the
  calendar-weighted duration masses sum to one for every interview month;
- baseline start-month multistart and recovery --- **passed provisionally**;
  three empirical conditional starts and distant simulated starts meet, and a
  2,000-record joint recovery gives month-distribution RMSE about 0.0044;
- baseline start-month predictive adequacy --- **passed for calendar months,
  failed for serial dependence**; 11 of 12 month shares and the whole-year
  revision rate are reproduced, but exact continuations remain too low and
  other revisions too high; and
- full 29-parameter observed-information inference --- **pending**; the
  gross-only January-heaping estimate is effectively on the boundary and
  should not receive a regular Wald interpretation;
- exact-anchor retention nesting and conditional identification --- **passed**;
  zero reproduces the flexible baseline likelihood exactly, the empirical
  profile has a clear interior maximum, and 20 conditional recovery samples
  recover the generating probability with small mean bias;
- exact-anchor predictive adequacy --- **failed but improved**; exact
  continuations rise from 60.6% to 61.8% against 64.7% observed and other
  revisions fall from 32.4% to 31.4% against 28.3% observed;
- longer 30-parameter multistart refinement --- **passed provisionally**;
  low- and high-retention screens are decisively inferior, a second joint
  block adds only 1.71 likelihood points, and the final conditional polish adds
  0.001 point, although the capped joint blocks retain convergence code 1;
- full 30-parameter recovery --- **passed for estimation and headline
  transition rates, inconclusive for the reporting decomposition**; three
  5,000-record samples give entry- and exit-rate RMSEs of about 0.12 and 0.11
  percentage points, while
  retention and the two revision probabilities remain noisy and offset one
  another;
- full-rank OPG analytical inference --- **passed provisionally**; the exact
  retention SE is 0.574 percentage points, but the information matrix is
  ill-conditioned, retention correlates 0.885 with tenure contamination, and
  gross-only January heaping is a boundary quantity; and
- exact central observed-information inference --- **pending**, with 48 of
  1,801 likelihood points cached;
- local-revision normalization and exact nesting --- **passed**; the
  one-to-six-month kernel renormalizes at zero tenure, excludes zero from its
  support, and setting its probability to zero reproduces the exact-anchor
  log likelihood exactly;
- local-revision conditional identification and multistart screening ---
  **passed provisionally**; the profile has a clear interior maximum, low and
  high starts are inferior, and central reporting-block refinement improves
  the preferred basin, although the deliberately capped blocks retain
  convergence code 1; and
- local-revision predictive adequacy --- **failed but substantially
  improved**; the predicted one-to-six-month share rises from 3.0% to 10.8%
  against 11.4% observed, and the likelihood gain is concentrated in records
  with local changes, but exact and residual-revision moments remain outside
  the simulation intervals;
- shared-reliability exact nesting and dispersed starts --- **passed
  provisionally**; zero dispersion reproduces the independent likelihood,
  all starts improve on it, and the preferred basin is clearly superior,
  although the short joint blocks terminate at their iteration caps;
- shared-reliability predictive adequacy --- **failed but informative**; the
  local-revision and zero/one-irregularity predictions improve, but the model
  overpredicts two irregularities and leaves several duration moments outside
  their simulation intervals; and
- cross-clock reliability interpretation --- **limited by the three-wave
  design**; within-clock clustering identifies the dispersions, but the data
  do not directly reveal repeated tenure and repeated timegap clocks for the
  same person;
- separate-dispersion joint convergence --- **passed**; broad reporting and
  transition blocks materially improve the initial fit, two cached joint
  continuations add 78.9 and 49.4 likelihood points, and a third returns the
  identical parameter vector with convergence code zero;
- fair common-dispersion refinement --- **passed**; projecting the converged
  nuisance block into the restricted model, polishing the common shift, and
  checking the full restricted score reduces the equality-restriction LR to
  144.6 without altering the transition rates;
- separate-dispersion recovery --- **passed provisionally**; one 10,000-person
  conditional recovery sample gives the same optimum from three starts and
  good latent-class discrimination, but more replications and full-nuisance
  recovery are still required;
- separate-dispersion OPG inference --- **passed numerically but limited for
  the restriction contrast**; the 33-parameter matrix is positive definite
  and full rank, but has condition number about 55 million, one hazard
  direction needs a smaller perturbation, and its Wald approximation conflicts
  with the directly optimized LR test; and
- separate-dispersion nuisance-adjusted profile inference --- **passed**; all
  retained points converge, two-start screens select the higher-likelihood
  warm branch on both sides, and the 95% profile interval for the
  timegap-minus-tenure dispersion is about 0.1100 to 0.1520, excluding the
  equality restriction and resolving the OPG/LR conflict in favor of the
  direct likelihood evidence; and
- separate-dispersion predictive adequacy --- **failed**; exact continuations
  improve modestly, but local revisions, residual revisions, timegap
  inconsistencies, and zero/one/two-irregularity shares remain outside the
  simulation intervals.
